cards.why: The v1 hat was judged BROKEN. v3_01 is the same iconic hat with a creased crown, band and curled brim, graded 3 and not broken. The producer has graded this object 3-5 before, so keep the object and use the clean drawing. Its green concentric-ring backdrop is still cool against the cream felt.

The gold pan got an outside grade of 2, and on its own it reads as a pie tin. Prospecting is not one of the genre's first-named objects. The v3 oil lantern is a classic frontier object with one compact body and a fire described the right way. If possible, move its backdrop from cyan to sky blue so cyan doesn't repeat across the set.
The producer graded the harmonica 5 before. It has a simple, distinctive silhouette, a real accent on the end covers, and the set's only pink backdrop.

It's the same boots-with-spurs plan in the same category and on the same purple floor, but v3_04 has an outside grade of 4 and v1_04 is ungraded. The star stitch is a real part that carries the accent. Go with the graded evidence.

The producer graded the saddle-on-hay-bale staging 2. In the v1 drawing only one stirrup reads and the saddle sits awkwardly on the bale. A saddle hung over a wooden fence rail is where it really rests and shows both stirrups hanging on either side. The object stays, which matters because it is iconic, and the backdrop stays cyan.
This is the strongest card on the evidence: outside grade 4 and producer grades 4, 5, 5. The saguaro is the genre's signature plant and the warm yellow backdrop sits against the green hero.

The producer graded the barrel 1. It's generic and only reads as western next to the other cards. The tumbleweed is pure western-film shorthand (outside grade 3) and reuses the sand ground from the cactus. That leaves the set without the house emblem, which is optional.

The covered wagon is a core iconic object, graded 3 outside and 4 and 3 by the producer. It has four wheels and its tongue rests on the ground, so it's buildable. As a category 3 card it stands on packed dirt, its real ground, on the green backdrop.

Keep the windmill, which the producer graded 4. Because its truss tower is a risky open frame, reword the subject to: 'a tall four-legged wooden windmill tower with cross braces, all four legs bolted to a square stone base, a round wheel of many metal blades on a hub at the top and a tail vane fixed behind the hub.' That pins down how the parts connect.
It's the same plan as v3_10, which was graded 3, and it uses the approved fire wording. It also gives the set its one night card with a warm light source. Keep it as is.

lessons.set_notes: After the swaps the set keeps its iconic core (hat, boots, saddle, cactus, covered wagon, windmill, campfire) and stays within the category rules: 3 in category 1, 1 in category 2, 4 in category 3 and 2 in category 4. It uses about six backdrops (green, cyan, pink, purple, warm yellow, night blue). Watch two things: cyan now repeats on the lantern, saddle and windmill, and the lantern and campfire both carry fire.

cards.why: The teacup is a core object for period drama and has a clean silhouette. It got a 3 here, matching the v1 and v2 teacups. The pale blue cup on a pink floor follows the cool-on-warm rule, and the gold rim is a real part that can carry the accent.

It got a 4, so keep the object. But the ribbon runs down the sides and ends in a bow, so the drawing reads as a gift box, not a hat box. Reword: 'A tall round hat box with a shallow flat lid overlapping the top edge and a cream cord handle looped through two holes in the lid; no ribbon on the body.' Colors: burgundy red, cream cord. The v2 Teapot was not taken because it would put a second tea item on the floor next to the teacup.

This is the highest grade in all three variants (5), and the hat is the most iconic object of the genre. The v2 grey hat was graded BROKEN, so keep this black hat with the red band on cyan exactly as planned.
The lace parasol is iconic and got a steady 3, as did the v2 parasol. A lavender canopy on yellow follows the cool-on-warm rule, and the wooden handle keeps its natural color.

The violin (3) is a generic music object that would not name period drama by itself. The pocket watch with its chain is a signature prop of the genre and is easy to read and build. Gold on fresh green follows the warm-on-cool rule, and it keeps category 1 at four cards.

The folding fan is a Regency staple with a simple silhouette that anyone can name. Red silk on sky blue follows the warm-on-cool rule. It is ungraded, but no graded alternative in the other variants is better.

A tiered afternoon-tea stand is specific to the genre, and it is a compact build: two plates on one post and foot. The rich purple backdrop and white linen surface follow the rules. It brings the tea world in without repeating the teacup.

The rounded lid, together with brass corners, reads as a pirate treasure chest, and the wood trunk blends into the wooden platform. Reword: 'A flat-topped rectangular steamer trunk with two leather straps buckled around it, brass corner guards, a brass latch at the front and a leather handle on each end, standing on a stone station platform.' Colors: wood brown, tan leather straps, brass gold, on sky blue.

A pearl strand is iconic jewelry for the genre and has a clear outline. It lies flat on a cushion, which correctly makes it category 3 with surface_from_above. White pearls against deep blue velvet give strong contrast.

The upright piano is the drawing-room centerpiece of the genre. It is a closed, compact body, with its keys and pedals where they work. It is the only category 4 card, and the plan follows that category's rules. The front door (graded 3 in v2) would be an equal swap, but it is not clearly better.

lessons.set_notes: The revised set is a coherent Regency/Victorian drawing-room-and-travel set. Its iconic core of top hat, teacup, parasol, fan and pocket watch matches the other variants, and the counts stay within the rules: 4 category 1, 2 category 2, 3 category 3 and 1 category 4. Backdrops span about seven clean hues: pink, green, cyan, yellow, sky blue, purple and orange. The two rewords stop the hat box and trunk from being read as a gift box and a treasure chest.

cards.why: Outside grade 3. It is a clear detective tool with one solid body, and the red body on cyan matches the backdrop rule.
The same press camera got grade 3 in two other variants (v1_03, v3_07). It is a compact, buildable body, and the sky-blue floating staging is right.

This card is BROKEN and graded 2. The flat map and the lying glass don't build. A magnifier is the genre's top icon, so keep it as a simple floating object instead. v3_01 also adds a grass-green backdrop the set needs. The swap moves the card from category 3 to category 1, which leaves 3 cards in each.
The fedora is a core genre icon, a simple garment, and correct as a category 2 card on a rich purple floor. The tan felt is warm against the cool purple.
The badge is a must-have icon. Showing it in an open wallet lying flat on the table is the right category 3 staging and keeps the outline precise. The card is ungraded, but it is plain and readable.
Outside grade 3. It is a flat object correctly on a surface viewed from above, and the gold ring partner object makes it read as evidence.

Plain yellow tape with no text is just a roll of tape and doesn't name the topic alone (grade 3). The steel safe is a compact, solid crime-story object graded 4, the best category 2 evidence. It keeps category 2 at 2 cards and brings a rich pink floor.
A fingerprint on a doorknob is the 'small object in its exact spot' card the rules ask for. The knob is a single solid on a plate, and the warm yellow backdrop adds variety.
Outside grade 4 is the strongest grade in the set. It is a vehicle on its own street, and the house pictogram on the door is the set's one emblem.
The same bloodhound was graded 3 in variant 1. It is the set's one animal and a recognizable sniffer dog, correctly on grass and last in the order.

lessons.set_notes: The two swaps replace the broken map card with a floating magnifier, the genre's top icon, and replace the anonymous tape roll with the 4-graded safe. The category counts become 3/2/3/2. Backdrops are cyan, sky blue, grass green, purple, pink and warm yellow, about six as the rules ask.
